newsitem.title: USA: FOREIGN SWEET CRUDES SEEN PLENTIFUL IN U.S. GULF.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN SWEET CRUDES SEEN PLENTIFUL IN U.S. GULF.

text.p: Asking prices for a variety of foreign sweet crudes offered in the U.S. Gulf Coast continued to soften on Thursday amid plentiful supplies, traders said.
Activity was subdued, with buyers generally reluctant to jump in as prices are dropping.
"I think people see plenty of oil out there and they say 'why rush?'" a Gulf Coast trader said.
Many traders were also hesitant to make any moves until Iraqi barrels start rolling out, probably by early next week.
Highlighting the decline in sweet prices, North Sea crude was indicated at around October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 40 cents a barrel for September 20-30 delivery into the U.S. Gulf.
The discount has steadily dropped from around 10 cents under WTI earlier this week, reflecting the sharp drop in Dated Brent, traders said.
A dated cargo for August 20-24 loading changed hands at September Brent minus 20 cents a barrel on Thursday, boosting the propsects for trans-Atlantic activity.
Among other North Sea crudes, a Norwegian company was offering a cargo of Heidrun for September 5-10 delivery, asking October WTI minus $1.00 a barrel.
A slew of West African cargoes were still looking for buyers in the Gulf, with Nigerian Qua Iboe offered around Dated Brent plus $1.90 a barrel.
The surfeit of sweet grades was also apparent in Latin America. A U.S. refiner was re-offering a Colombian Cusiana cargo loading September 14-18, asking around October WTI minus 70 cents a barrel.
Elsewhere in the region, traders were awaiting the results of Petroperu's tender to buy 380,000 barrels of crude for August 29-31 arrival on a cif or fob basis.
